description.narrative: Empowered communities, improved stakeholder cooperation and synergised planning for restoration of riverscapes in Meghna-Barak River Basin, providing a learning opportunity on how multi-level stakeholder cooperation can result in inclusive, sustainable, and ecosystem-based river governance. Specific Objectives • Identify competing interests and synergies among communities, government, and private sector actors to build consensus on sustainable river governance. • Co-develop inclusive People’s River Plans that reflect community knowledge, technical analysis, and responsible private sector roles. • Establish sustained dialogue platforms and build local capacity to implement river restoration plans and foster regional cooperation. • Strengthen nationalinstitutions to integrate community perspectives into planning and align with the UN Water Convention. Project Phases: The project will run for 12 months (November 2025 – October 2026), structured in three overlapping phases. While each phase contributesto specific outcomes, Outcome 4 (strengthening national institutions and aligning with the UN Water Convention) is cross- cutting and embedded throughout the project. National actors such as WARPO, the Joint Rivers Commission, BWDB, and relevant ministries will be engaged in each phase to ensure that participatory processes influence formal planning and regulatory frameworks at multiple levels. Participatory Assessments and Evidence Generation: initial assessments and dialogues will generate evidence and surface community priorities, while engaging national institutions early through orientation sessions and technical briefings on the project’s participatory and transboundary approach. Consensus-Building and Planning: Co-development of People’s RiverPlans will bring together community knowledge, technical evidence, and national policy frameworks. National agencies will be involved in dialogue processes and supported to explore how participatory planning can inform master plans, Delta Plan implementation, and cross-sector coordination. Peer exchange with Dutch institutions will begin. Institutionalisation and Piloting: Dialogue platforms will be formalised, and local-to-national linkages strengthened through targeted capacity support. National agencies will receive training and technical input aligned with the UN Water Convention, while twinning and exchange activities with Dutch knowledge institutions will help institutionalise new practices. Pilot restoration effortswill generate learning for long-term uptake. Communications and Dissemination: The project will implement a comprehensive communications strategy to ensure visibility, transparency, and stakeholder engagement. Social media will be used before and after each dialogue or activity to share announcements, highlights, and outcomes. Draft People’s River Plans will be published both online and offline for citizen and stakeholder feedback. Finalised plans and policy briefs will be widely disseminated to communities, institutions,and relevantplatforms. Pilot initiatives will be supported by targeted communications activities to mobilise awareness and strengthen community-led action. Sustainability: The project is designed to ensure that its impacts extend beyond the implementation period.People’s River Plans will provide reference documents for CSOs, community leaders, and local institutions to influence mainstream processes such as the Haor Master Plan, Annual Development Plans, and longer-term sectoral strategies. To secure continuity,theprojectwill foster multi-stakeholder and diversified funding mechanisms by engaging local governments, line ministries, and the private sector. Oxfam will also provide ongoing technical engagement with government institutions, ensuring that lessons and tools from the pilots are integrated into Master Plan implementation and related policy frameworks.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project#s implementation.
